rooms.name: West of House
rooms.text: You are standing in a field. You see a boarded up house, a mailbox, and a clear sky.

looks.text: You see a black mailbox with a little red flag, a rusty mailbox door, and the mailbox is labeled in white paint: 'memory', with presumably the house number, '2112'.

triggers.say: This journal seems magical. You don't know how the mechanism works. As you lift the journal to peer more closely at it, a slip of lumpy folded paper falls out onto the ground.
The paper unfolds in your hands. It's a map.

entries.summary: The Royal Society's secretary printed the letters scientists sent him. It's the oldest science journal still in print.

rooms.name: Front of House
rooms.text: You see that the house is made of bricks, some of which are crumbling or missing. The door is boarded up, but not well.

triggers.say: *There is a two-fold Silence*. You hear the rush of the sea and a wave crashing on the shore. But inside you see only a normal, though dimly-lit, room.

rooms.name: Front Room
rooms.text: There is a small, sturdy, wooden desk. On top of it is a metal box, with a row of dials and 3 ports. One of the ports holds the jack of one side of an electrical cord. A glass jar sits beside it, sealed with a thick rubber stopper, and with a brass rod sticking straight up through the stopper.

looks.text: Inside the jar are two impossibly thin ribbons of gold foil hanging side by side. You hear a hum from the metal box, and the electrical cord shakes.
One side of the cord is connected to the metal box with the knobs. The other end exposes a metal tip.

triggers.say: You hear a hum and a crack, and the 2 foils in the jar move apart.

entries.summary: Two gold leaves given the same charge push apart. Bennet called it the most sensible electrometer yet constructed.
entries.long_text: New Experiments on Electricity, wherein the causes of THUNDER and LIGHTNING as well as the constant state of Pofitive or negative Electricity in the Air or Clouds, are explained; with Experiments on Clouds of Powders and Vapours artificially diffused in the air. Also a description of A DOUBLER of ELECTRICITY, and of the most SENSIBLE ELECTROMETER YET CONSTRUCTED, with other New Experiments and Difcoveries in the Science, illustrated by explanatory plates.
